testingFrequency: Online submission required for backflow test reports
dueBasis: Baytown requires online submission of Backflow Prevention Assembly Test and Maintenance Reports through Envirotrax, with testing information entered directly by the tester into the online system.
officialListLabel: View Baytown testers registered with Envirotrax

submissionMethods.label: Envirotrax online backflow and CSI submission

penalties: Baytown says testers no longer submit paper test reports directly to the City; backflow and CSI reporting are routed through Envirotrax.
sourceExcerpt: Baytown requires online Envirotrax submission for backflow test reports, provides an Envirotrax registered tester route, and also routes licensed CSI inspector reports to Envirotrax.
verdictSummary: Baytown is a strong Envirotrax utility because both backflow test reports and CSI reports run through the online system instead of paper submission.
whoIsAffected: Baytown customers with backflow prevention assemblies, commercial CSI requirements, and fire protection sprinkler assemblies.
residentialNotes: Residential owners should confirm whether a backflow assembly is on file before scheduling.
If testing is required, the tester submits through Envirotrax rather than direct paper delivery.
commercialNotes: Commercial customers may also need CSI reports, which Baytown routes through Envirotrax.
Fire protection sprinkler assemblies require BPATs who satisfy the State Fire Marshal employment rule.

annualTesting.summary: Baytown's public page is strongest on the accepted submission path: backflow test and maintenance reports must be entered in Envirotrax.
highlights: Paper reports are no longer submitted directly to the City.
Registered tester lookup is tied to Envirotrax.
workflowSteps: Confirm the assembly and report requirement with Baytown.
Use a tester registered with Envirotrax.
Have the tester submit the report through the online system.

irrigation.summary: Baytown's public page does not isolate irrigation rules, so irrigation users should verify whether the assembly is reportable and then follow the Envirotrax submission path.
highlights: A registered tester should complete the report.
workflowSteps: Confirm whether the irrigation assembly is on file.
Submit through Envirotrax if testing is required.

fireLine.summary: Baytown states fire protection sprinkler assemblies must be tested or repaired by a BPAT who is a full-time employee of a licensed fire protection sprinkler company.
highlights: Fire protection sprinkler assemblies are called out separately.
State Fire Marshal licensing context matters.
Envirotrax remains the backflow reporting route.
workflowSteps: Identify whether the assembly serves a fire protection sprinkler system.
Use a BPAT who satisfies the fire sprinkler employment rule.
Use Baytown's official page to confirm whether the assembly or CSI record is required.
Find a tester registered with Envirotrax.
Have the tester or licensed CSI inspector submit through Envirotrax.
Do not rely on paper reports submitted directly to the City.
failureHighlights: Paper test reports are no longer the direct City submission route.
Licensed CSI reports also go through Envirotrax.
Fire protection sprinkler assemblies need the State Fire Marshal employment overlay.

costBand.testingRange: Private Baytown pricing varies by assembly and whether CSI is involved.
costBand.repairRetestRange: Repair and retest costs depend on assembly type and fire-line status.
costBand.pricingNotes: The practical cost risk is using a tester or CSI inspector who does not complete the Envirotrax submission.
